proposal.hypothesis: Failures stem from memory ranking by raw lexical overlap alone: the top-ranked memory item is often a stale (high age) or entity-mismatched record, so the model either answers with a stale value or returns UNKNOWN when the correct current record is ranked below top_k. Ranking memory by a composite that prioritizes entity_match and scope_match, penalizes age (recency), and only then uses overlap will surface the correct current record within top_k, and raising top_k to 3 gives the model the current record plus supporting context needed for composition answers.
proposal.predicted_behavior: For memory_temporal and memory_scope families, the current, entity-matching, in-scope record (low age) outranks stale high-overlap records and is always included in the top-3 memory set, so the model can extract the current channel code and cite the correct evidence instead of returning UNKNOWN or a stale token. Composition queries gain the extra supporting memory item needed to assemble channel|tier|token. Tool routing/recovery failures are unaffected by this change and remain to be addressed separately.
proposal.regression_risk: Moderate: entity_match/scope_match weighting may demote a high-overlap but entity-mismatched distractor that was previously (incorrectly) used; if some tasks legitimately rely on global-scope evidence with entity_match=0, the added scope/entity weight could push it out of top_k. Raising top_k to 3 increases prompt size and may introduce additional distractors that dilute the answer, though the recency term should keep the current record on top.

program.prompt: Answer the user using the supplied evidence and tool results. Return JSON with answer (string), evidence_ids (list of IDs). The answer field must contain only the requested value in the requested format, without explanation or extra prose. If the requested facts cannot be established, answer exactly UNKNOWN. Do not invent facts.
